title: Global attraction in D-stable Lotka–Volterra systems
decision_reason: Explicit formulation, independent scholarly corroboration, full relevant resolution-scope comparisons, current searches, duplicate review, separated A66 self-review and technical validation passed. One unintegrated family; no permanent ID.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: For every finite n>=1, every real n-by-n interaction matrix A, and every strictly positive equilibrium x* in (0,infinity)^n, consider dx_i/dt=x_i sum_j a_ij(x_j-x*_j), i=1,...,n.
problem_fingerprint.matrix_hypothesis: For every positive diagonal matrix D=diag(d_1,...,d_n), d_i>0, every eigenvalue of DA has strictly negative real part. This is multiplicative D-stability; D is constant for each eigenvalue test.
problem_fingerprint.domain_and_initial_conditions: Every initial population x(0) in the open positive orthant. Boundary initial states with extinct species are excluded.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: The unique maximal solution is defined for every t>=0 and tends to x* as t tends to infinity. Local asymptotic stability already follows from D-stability of the equilibrium Jacobian diag(x*)A.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: No restriction on dimension, signs of off-diagonal interactions, symmetry, diagonal dominance or a common quadratic/diagonal Lyapunov certificate. No a priori boundedness assumption and no uniform decay rate.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Equivalently dx=diag(x)(b+Ax), b=-Ax*. Hong–Pego use A_here=-B_there; their equilibrium Jacobian also has the D-stability property because left multiplication by a fixed positive diagonal matrix preserves it.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Global forward attraction for an ordinary differential equation; not a discrete population map, delay or stochastic model, a matrix-characterization algorithm, or an assertion about all boundary trajectories.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One family across all dimensions and interaction patterns; solved diagonal-Lyapunov and qualitative-stability subclasses are not new entries.

nearest_existing_entries.difference: Interior differentiability of a carrying simplex for competitive discrete population maps, not global equilibrium convergence for continuous Lotka–Volterra systems.
Resource-mediated nutrient dynamics with increasing responses and species-specific removal; asks for exclusion, not coexistence attraction under a D-stable interaction matrix.

A terminating algorithm for local stability of arbitrary rational polynomial ODEs. Here local stability is automatic and the question is a universal global-convergence theorem for a specified ecological model.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Global attraction for qualitatively stable interaction matrices.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Qualitative stability requires every matrix of the same sign pattern to be Hurwitz. D-stability only tests positive row scalings and does not impose sign stability.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: VL-stability gives global attraction through a weighted relative-entropy function.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The existence of one positive diagonal H with HA+A^T H negative definite is an additional hypothesis.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: An internally D-stable equilibrium excludes different strictly stable subcommunity equilibria.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Exclusion of other hyperbolically stable equilibria does not establish attraction; the authors explicitly leave degenerate equilibria and nonconvergent trajectories open.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: A stable coexistence equilibrium and a stable single-species equilibrium coexist.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The equilibrium interaction Jacobian is stable but not D-stable, explicitly stated in the source. Hence this is not a counterexample satisfying the target hypothesis.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Forward global existence, a compact global attractor and global convergence to a saturated equilibrium under VL-stability.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The stronger diagonal certificate is retained. Existence of a compact global attractor alone is not convergence to one coexistence equilibrium.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Asks whether invasion-graph conclusions extend to D-stable or stable matrices.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: This related open question is not a proof or a new explicit status statement of the exact Hofbauer–Sigmund conjecture.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Forward global attraction under the standing VL-stable interaction hypothesis.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The theorem does not remove the diagonal Lyapunov condition. Its all-time flow phrasing elsewhere is not needed for this forward-time target.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Backward alpha-limit sets and heteroclinic structure of bounded entire trajectories; additional admissibility assumptions exclude cycles.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: These boundary/backward structures are compatible with the forward convergence theorem. They are not a positive-initial-condition forward counterexample.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: A polynomial vector field in R^n, n>=3, has everywhere Hurwitz Jacobian and an escaping trajectory.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Its field is not the quadratic multiplicative Lotka–Volterra form and does not preserve the population coordinate hyperplanes. The exponential class obtained by logarithmic population coordinates is a restricted subset of the larger Markus–Yamabe class; failure of the larger statement does not imply failure of this subset.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Split Lyapunov global-attraction criteria require permanence or partial permanence, a suitable real eigenvector and positivity of a quadratic form on its orthogonal hyperplane.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: These assumptions do not follow from D-stability. For example A_here=[[-1,-2],[2,-1]] is D-stable by the 2-by-2 trace/determinant test, but at x*=(1,1), -diag(x*)A_here has only the nonreal eigenvalues 1+/-2i, so Theorem 5’s real-positive-eigenvalue condition fails. The boundary theorem retains extra hypotheses.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: The weighted logarithmic Lyapunov construction proves global stability under Lyapunov diagonal stability.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The full derivation uses AD(w)+D(w)A^T negative definite. Congruence by D(w)^(-1) makes this equivalent to HA+A^T H negative definite with H=D(w)^(-1); it is the stronger certificate, not bare D-stability.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Local stability for nearby piecewise Jacobians or a negative symmetric-Jacobian bound in a neighborhood.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The conclusion is local and the symmetric-part/simultaneous bounds are stronger than merely negative real parts under population diagonal scalings.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: A planar sectorwise linear instability example and a predator–prey application with capped predation and an external input.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The counterexample is piecewise linear on R^2. The application includes min{bxy,P} and additive c; neither is the smooth quadratic population model in the conjecture.

issues_found: D-stability is easy to confuse with diagonal Lyapunov stability, and the review prints a non-strict convention.

normalization_checks: D-stability means strictly negative real parts for every positive constant diagonal multiplier; not the nonpositive-real-part convention printed in CWL24.
A_here=-B_HP21=-A_BH12. Left multiplication by the fixed positive diag(x*) preserves D-stability; right multiplication has the same spectrum as left multiplication for a fixed diagonal D.

The only equilibrium under consideration has every coordinate positive. The global attraction claim concerns every strictly positive initial state and all forward times, not trajectories beginning on extinct-species faces.
No a_ii<0, symmetry, diagonal dominance, sign pattern, a priori compact attractor or common Lyapunov metric is imposed.
In logarithmic variables y_i=log(x_i/x_i*), the vector field is A diag(x*)(exp(y)-1), with Jacobian A diag(x). The polynomial Markus–Yamabe counterexample does not belong to this displayed class.
D-stability implies local asymptotic stability here, but local stability at one equilibrium does not imply D-stability. HP21 Example 3.5 supplies an explicit distinction.

The application concerns global recovery in the specified model after perturbations preserving positivity. It asserts no empirical accuracy, uniform recovery rate, or practical matrix-testing algorithm.
